judgment.summary: The crossword teaches ten real AI concepts (tools, memory, agents, context, skills, loops, graphs, projects) with correctly scoped, honestly hedged mechanisms, plain adult-beginner language, and Rewind Era references that each do double duty. Action labels and hint links name actual destinations (the LIBRAiRY, Mme CLAi-O, the NewsStand), banned wording is absent, brand spellings are exact, and both house ads land jokes that restate their destination's teaching. Judged within the necessarily repeated clue/hint/explanation form, the explanations vary in shape and voice rather than following a template. Remaining items are uncertainties (PAIGE/"Useful this week" not in canon, unverifiable link anchors and game status), not confirmed failures.
qualityFindings: PAIGE as a NewsStand reporter and the 'Useful this week' section are not confirmable from the canon file, which lists only publications (The Breaking, The Daily, The Weekly, The Tribune) and named characters; nothing retired is used, so this is named as an uncertainty, not a defect.
Link anchors (e.g. /library.html#ai-fundamentals-101::%40chapter-14) and the live status of the Mme CLAi-O game cannot be verified from prose; the copy itself makes no false availability claim.

The LIBRAiRY house ad link 'Find your next explanation →' is the weakest label on the page — the kicker and headline name the destination, but the link itself edges toward generic 'Learn more' territory; naming the LIBRAiRY in the link would be stronger.

The CLAIO clue ('the SUNNYVAiLE reading is a reflection, not a weather forecast') is the hardest entry for a newcomer who hasn't met Mme CLAi-O, though the hint, the in-town link, and crossings make it fair; the grid entry CLAIO is a normal crossword flattening of the branded CLAi-O, which the explanation restores.

Chapter mapping is internally consistent (TOOLS/AGENTS/LOOPS to the agents chapter, SKILLS/GRAPH to chapter 15, CONTEXT/PROJECTS to working-with-ai-101), reinforcing the concepts as a connected set rather than isolated trivia.
judgment.readerChange: A reader leaves able to do specific things, not just define words: check which route an AI took to a number, review and edit what a product has saved in memory, decide which agent actions need approval before a goal starts, supply missing context instead of assuming the AI can see a filed document, read a skill's actual instructions before trusting its name, trace a workflow graph for a human-approval step before anything sends, and give a looping agent a stopping point. The closing 'ideas to recognize, not a test of which AI subscriptions you own' framing plus hedged feature language ('in products that offer this feature') keeps her from misapplying advice to a product that lacks the feature.
judgment.voiceComparison: This reads like Episode 1's voice adapted to puzzle scale: useful before clever, references that carry the lesson rather than decorate it (the Spice Girls line teaches that memory retains things you might not want retained; 'Groundhog Day would make a terrible project plan' motivates stopping conditions the way the Burn Book motivates hallucination checking), and honest limits stated plainly ('Saved information is not necessarily included in every answer'). 'A goal is not a blank cheque' and 'the name on the package is not the instructions inside' are the same aphoristic-but-mechanistic register as 'Polished is a style. Evidence is a standard.' The house ads hit the Episode 1 bar exactly — 'Be kind. Rewind. Look it up.' and the voicemail line are period-precise jokes that restate the destination's teaching. No banned patterns, no template smell, AI is consistently 'it,' and the reader is treated as smart and busy rather than sorted into beginner/expert camps.
